page.title: Templates
page.purpose: Let an operator see how generated documents are allowed to look — what each template can honor on each target, which brand tokens it binds, which documents it governs — and decide template changes with the blast radius visible before, not after.

priorities.statement: What a template can actually honor is stated per target, not inferred from its name.
priorities.notes: A deck template that supports speaker notes in .pptx and not in PDF is telling the truth about both. Fidelity is a declaration; a target with no declaration is refused rather than attempted.

priorities.statement: A template switch shows what will be lost before it commits.
priorities.notes: This is the highest-weight moment on this surface. A silent drop during a switch is the write-side equivalent of an anchor that lies, and the operator finds out from the audience.

priorities.statement: The blast radius of a template edit is visible on the edit.
priorities.notes: A per-document override and a template edit read identically as intentions. They differ by how many documents change, including ones already sent — so the count belongs on the decision, not in a confirmation dialog's small print.

priorities.statement: Presentation is shown as bound tokens, never as literal values.
priorities.notes: A template carrying a literal color or font drifts from brand permanently and silently. Showing bindings rather than swatches makes the rule legible instead of merely enforced.

states.description: Templates are listed with their declared targets, fidelity per target, brand bindings and the number of documents each governs.
No templates exist yet; the primary action is creating one, which requires declaring at least one target and its fidelity.
A proposed template edit is awaiting a human decision, with the count of affected documents shown.
A specific spec is being previewed under a different template, with unrepresentable elements and unhonored overrides listed before anything commits.
Template validation or a switch preview failed, naming which terminal state applies.

elements.name: Templates
elements.description: Each row shows declared targets and the number of documents governed.

elements.name: Fidelity by target
elements.description: Which of paged-geometry, cell-structure, speaker-notes, vector-embed and styled-text the template honors for each declared target.

elements.name: Brand token bindings
elements.description: The tokens this template's presentation references. Literal values are a validation failure, not a row.

elements.name: Proposed edits

elements.name: What this switch changes
elements.description: Unrepresentable elements and overrides the target template cannot honor.

claims.statement: The templates page exposes a named registry region.
Every template shows its declared fidelity for each target it claims.
A target a template does not declare is presented as unavailable, never offered as a best-effort attempt.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-016. no_renderer_for_target is a roadmap item and renderer_unavailable is a one-command fix; offering an undeclared target collapses that distinction into a failure the operator cannot act on.

claims.statement: Template presentation is displayed as brand-token bindings rather than literal color or font values.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-013. A literal in a template is a validation failure precisely so a rebrand is a corpus-wide re-render rather than a corpus-wide template edit. Showing bindings makes the invariant visible instead of merely enforced.

claims.statement: A template switch lists every unrepresentable element and every override the target cannot honor, before the commit action is available.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-014 and OT-P2-015. This is the load-bearing moment of the surface. Committing first and reporting after means the operator discovers the loss from the audience.

claims.statement: A proposed template edit shows how many documents it would change, on the decision itself.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-024. An override and a template edit are indistinguishable as intentions and differ only in blast radius, so the count is the thing that makes the decision a real one.

claims.statement: A proposed template edit is never applied without an explicit human decision, and the decision is recorded.
claims.rationale: Mirrors the redaction-review pattern already in this scenario, for the same reason: an automated change with corpus-wide reach is not defensible after the fact.

claims.statement: Forking to a new template is offered wherever editing an existing one is.
Empty, populated, proposal-pending, switch-preview and error states are all reachable and distinct.
Template navigation, the fidelity matrix, the proposal queue and the switch confirmation are reachable by keyboard alone.
